source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament; complete Acts
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360). NB Codex Bezae (D/05; 5th c.) preserves a notably different 'Western' text of Acts — Acts has the most dramatic text-type divergence in the NT, with the 'Western' text (Bezae + Old Latin + Cyprianic citations) roughly 8.5% longer than the 'Alexandrian' text (Vaticanus + Sinaiticus). Bezae Western variants are documented per verse.
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P45 (Chester Beatty I; 3rd c. CE) preserves substantial portions of Acts. P74 (7th c.) preserves much of Acts but is comparatively late. For Acts 2 specifically, no 2nd-c. papyrus survives; the earliest substantial witnesses are P45 + the 4th-c. uncials Vaticanus + Sinaiticus.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017). For Western-text divergences: Boismard-Lamouille *Le texte occidental des Actes des Apôtres* (1984).
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bezae (Western) + P45 original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus + Boismard-Lamouille Western edition
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + Metzger UBS Textual Commentary (2nd ed. 1994) ad loc.
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Metzger, B. M., *A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament*, 2nd ed. (UBS 1994). Boismard, M.-É. & Lamouille, A., *Le texte occidental des Actes des Apôtres* (Paris 1984). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c.). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + (4th c.). Codex Bezae: Cambridge UL Nn.II.41 (5th c.). Barrett ICC 1994-1998; Bock BECNT 2007; Bruce NICNT 1988; Conzelmann Hermeneia 1987; Fitzmyer AB 1998; Haenchen 1971; Johnson SP 1992; Keener 2012-2015 (4-vol megaproject); Pervo Hermeneia 2009; Witherington 1998; Talbert 2005; Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT (Alexandrian text-type). Western-text variants per Codex Bezae are documented per verse where significant. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated in the uncials.

verses.text: Καὶ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς ἦσαν πάντες ὁμοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.
verses.translit: Kai en tō symplērousthai tēn hēmeran tēs pentēkostēs ēsan pantes homou epi to auto.
verses.notes: **PENTECOST OPENING**. *pentēkostē* = Pentecost / Shavuot — the Festival of Weeks (Lev 23:15-21; Deut 16:9-12), the second of the three pilgrim-feasts, fifty days after Passover. By the 1st c. CE Jewish tradition associated Shavuot with the Sinai theophany / giving of the Torah (cf. Jubilees 1:1; b. Pesah. 68b) — this background frames the Acts 2 fire+wind+voice manifestation as a new Sinai. *epi to auto* (in one place / together) is a recurring Lukan-Acts community-formula (cf. 1:15; 2:44, 47). Barrett ICC 1.110-113; Fitzmyer AB 233-235.

verses.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἄφνω ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἦχος ὥσπερ φερομένης πνοῆς βιαίας καὶ ἐπλήρωσεν ὅλον τὸν οἶκον οὗ ἦσαν καθήμενοι·
verses.translit: kai egeneto aphnō ek tou ouranou ēchos hōsper pheromenēs pnoēs biaias kai eplērōsen holon ton oikon hou ēsan kathēmenoi·
verses.notes: **MAJOR THEOPHANIC MANIFESTATION — SOUND/WIND**. *aphnō* (suddenly). *ek tou ouranou* (from heaven / from the sky). *ēchos* (sound). *hōsper pheromenēs pnoēs biaias* (as of a violently-borne wind). Cross-corpus 1 Kgs 19:11-12 (Elijah at Horeb — wind theophany); Exod 19:16-19 (Sinai — thunders + voice + smoke + earthquake); Ezek 1:4 (storm-wind from the north); Ezek 37:9-10 (the four winds animating the dry bones); 2 Bar 21:6. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward (a) conventional Spirit-as-wind theology, (b) Sinai-typology theophany reading, or (c) Raëlian readings of *ēchos ek tou ouranou* as craft-sound; preserve the surface.

verses.text: καὶ ὤφθησαν αὐτοῖς διαμεριζόμεναι γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐφ’ ἕνα ἕκαστον αὐτῶν,
verses.translit: kai ōphthēsan autois diamerizomenai glōssai hōsei pyros, kai ekathisen eph’ hena hekaston autōn,
verses.notes: **MAJOR THEOPHANIC MANIFESTATION — TONGUES OF FIRE**. *glōssai hōsei pyros* (tongues like fire — note the simile *hōsei*, 'as it were'). *diamerizomenai* (being distributed / divided). *ekathisen* (singular — settled). Cross-corpus Exod 19:18 (Sinai descending in fire); Exod 3:2 (burning bush); Num 11:25 (Spirit-distribution to the 70 elders); 1 Enoch 14:8-25 (throne-vision fire); 1QS 4:20-21 (Qumran spirit-of-truth). **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the *glōssai hōsei pyros* image is heavily engaged in heterodox traditions and explicitly in the Raëlian canon as a craft/laser manifestation. Preserve the simile-surface; do not pre-resolve toward (a) conventional Spirit-fire theology, (b) Sinai-typology, or (c) Raëlian craft-reading.

verses.text: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες πνεύματος ἁγίου, καὶ ἤρξαντο λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γλώσσαις καθὼς τὸ πνεῦμα ἐδίδου ἀποφθέγγεσθαι αὐτοῖς.
verses.translit: kai eplēsthēsan pantes pneumatos hagiou, kai ērxanto lalein heterais glōssais kathōs to pneuma edidou apophthengesthai autois.
verses.notes: **GLOSSOLALIA AT PENTECOST**. *heterais glōssais* (in other tongues / languages) — the Acts 2 phenomenon is presented as xenolalia (intelligible foreign languages, vv.6-11) rather than the ecstatic glossolalia of 1 Cor 14. *apophthengesthai* (utter / declare oracularly) — a vocabulary-choice with oracular / prophetic resonance (LXX 1 Chr 25:1; Ezek 13:9; Mic 5:11).

verses.text: Ἦσαν δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι, ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν·
verses.translit: Ēsan de eis Ierousalēm katoikountes Ioudaioi, andres eulabeis apo pantos ethnous tōn hypo ton ouranon·
verses.notes: *Ioudaioi* (Judeans / Jews) + *eulabeis* (devout). *apo pantos ethnous tōn hypo ton ouranon* (from every nation under heaven) — universalizing scope, framing the table-of-nations catalogue vv.9-11. Variant: some Western witnesses + Bezae omit *Ioudaioi*, making the audience purely Gentile pilgrims; the standard reading preserves the diaspora-Jewish framing.

verses.text: γενομένης δὲ τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης συνῆλθε τὸ πλῆθος καὶ συνεχύθη, ὅτι ἤκουον εἷς ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ λαλούντων αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: genomenēs de tēs phōnēs tautēs synēlthe to plēthos kai synechythē, hoti ēkouon heis hekastos tē idia dialektō lalountōn autōn.
verses.notes: *synechythē* (was confounded) — Lukan wordplay reversing Babel (Gen 11:7-9 LXX uses cognate *synechythē* for the confusion of languages). Pentecost as Babel-reversal is a major patristic + modern reading-theme.

verses.text: ἐξίσταντο δὲ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον λέγοντες· Οὐχ ἰδοὺ πάντες οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ λαλοῦντες Γαλιλαῖοι;
verses.translit: existanto de kai ethaumazon legontes· Ouch idou pantes houtoi eisin hoi lalountes Galilaioi?
verses.notes: *Galilaioi* — Galileans, a rural dialect-group whose Aramaic was notably distinct (cf. Matt 26:73 Peter's accent). The wonder-frame: how can these rustics speak our languages?

verses.text: καὶ πῶς ἡμεῖς ἀκούομεν ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ ἡμῶν ἐν ᾗ ἐγεννήθημεν;
verses.translit: kai pōs hēmeis akouomen hekastos tē idia dialektō hēmōn en hē egennēthēmen?
verses.notes: *tē idia dialektō* (one's own native language). The 'language-of-birth' specification frames the xenolalia / hearing-miracle ambiguity (debated since patristics: is the miracle in the speakers' tongues or in the hearers' ears?).

verses.text: Πάρθοι καὶ Μῆδοι καὶ Ἐλαμῖται, καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν, Ἰουδαίαν τε καὶ Καππαδοκίαν, Πόντον καὶ τὴν Ἀσίαν,
verses.translit: Parthoi kai Mēdoi kai Elamitai, kai hoi katoikountes tēn Mesopotamian, Ioudaian te kai Kappadokian, Ponton kai tēn Asian,
verses.notes: TABLE OF NATIONS — part 1. The list moves roughly east-to-west: Parthians, Medes, Elamites (Persian-empire successors), Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia (= Roman province). The inclusion of Ioudaian is geographically odd in a diaspora-list; Augustine and others proposed emendations; modern scholarship treats it as authentic (Lukan emphasis on universal-from-Jerusalem).

verses.text: Φρυγίαν τε καὶ Παμφυλίαν, Αἴγυπτον καὶ τὰ μέρη τῆς Λιβύης τῆς κατὰ Κυρήνην, καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες Ῥωμαῖοι,
verses.translit: Phrygian te kai Pamphylian, Aigypton kai ta merē tēs Libyēs tēs kata Kyrēnēn, kai hoi epidēmountes Rhōmaioi,
verses.notes: TABLE OF NATIONS — part 2. Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, the region of Libya about Cyrene, and the visiting Romans. *epidēmountes* (sojourning / visiting) — pilgrim-visitor distinction. The Cyrenian-Jewish community will reappear (6:9; 11:20; 13:1).

verses.text: Ἰουδαῖοί τε καὶ προσήλυτοι, Κρῆτες καὶ Ἄραβες, ἀκούομεν λαλούντων αὐτῶν ταῖς ἡμετέραις γλώσσαις τὰ μεγαλεῖα τοῦ θεοῦ.
verses.translit: Ioudaioi te kai prosēlytoi, Krētes kai Arabes, akouomen lalountōn autōn tais hēmeterais glōssais ta megaleia tou theou.
verses.notes: TABLE OF NATIONS — closing. *prosēlytoi* (proselytes — Gentile converts to Judaism). Cretans + Arabs (Nabataeans). *ta megaleia tou theou* (the mighty acts of God) — cross-corpus LXX Ps 70:19; Sir 36:7; 42:21. The xenolalic content is doxology-praise rather than evangelical-proclamation.

verses.text: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες καὶ διηπόρουν, ἄλλος πρὸς ἄλλον λέγοντες· Τί θέλει τοῦτο εἶναι;
verses.translit: existanto de pantes kai diēporoun, allos pros allon legontes· Ti thelei touto einai?
verses.notes: *diēporoun* (were perplexed). The *ti thelei touto einai* ("what does this mean?") sets up Peter's interpretive speech.

verses.text: ἕτεροι δὲ διαχλευάζοντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Γλεύκους μεμεστωμένοι εἰσίν.
verses.translit: heteroi de diachleuazontes elegon hoti Gleukous memestōmenoi eisin.
verses.notes: *gleukos* (sweet new wine — fresh unfermented grape-juice in some uses, but in this context the still-fermenting must with high alcohol content). The drunkenness-charge sets up Peter's v.15 rebuttal.

verses.text: Σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος σὺν τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐπῆρεν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπεφθέγξατο αὐτοῖς· Ἄνδρες Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες Ἰερουσαλὴμ πάντες, τοῦτο ὑμῖν γνωστὸν ἔστω καὶ ἐνωτίσασθε τὰ ῥήματά μου.
verses.translit: Statheis de ho Petros syn tois hendeka epēren tēn phōnēn autou kai apephthenxato autois· Andres Ioudaioi kai hoi katoikountes Ierousalēm pantes, touto hymin gnōston estō kai enōtisasthe ta rhēmata mou.
verses.notes: **PETER'S PENTECOST SPEECH — OPENING**. The first major sermon of Acts. *syn tois hendeka* (with the eleven) — collegial framing. *apephthenxato* — same oracular vocabulary as v.4. *enōtisasthe* (give ear) — biblical-prophetic call-to-attention idiom (LXX Isa 1:2; Joel 1:2).

verses.text: οὐ γὰρ ὡς ὑμεῖς ὑπολαμβάνετε οὗτοι μεθύουσιν, ἔστιν γὰρ ὥρα τρίτη τῆς ἡμέρας,
verses.translit: ou gar hōs hymeis hypolambanete houtoi methyousin, estin gar hōra tritē tēs hēmeras,
verses.notes: *hōra tritē* (third hour) = ~9 AM by Jewish reckoning. The morning-prayer hour, before the standard mid-day meal — too early for drunkenness.

verses.text: ἀλλὰ τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ εἰρημένον διὰ τοῦ προφήτου Ἰωήλ·
verses.translit: alla touto estin to eirēmenon dia tou prophētou Iōēl·
verses.notes: **JOEL-CITATION FORMULA**. Peter introduces the Joel 2:28-32 LXX citation (= Joel 3:1-5 in MT numbering). *touto estin to eirēmenon* — pesher-style identification formula ("this is that which") familiar from Qumran (1QpHab) and early Christian midrash.

verses.text: Καὶ ἔσται ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις, λέγει ὁ θεός, ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν καὶ αἱ θυγατέρες ὑμῶν, καὶ οἱ νεανίσκοι ὑμῶν ὁράσεις ὄψονται, καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ὑμῶν ἐνύπνια ἐνυπνιασθήσονται·
verses.translit: Kai estai en tais eschatais hēmerais, legei ho theos, ekcheō apo tou pneumatos mou epi pasan sarka, kai prophēteusousin hoi huioi hymōn kai hai thygateres hymōn, kai hoi neaniskoi hymōn horaseis opsontai, kai hoi presbyteroi hymōn enypnia enypniasthēsontai·
verses.notes: **JOEL 2:28 LXX (3:1 MT) CITATION**. Peter substitutes *en tais eschatais hēmerais* (in the last days) for the LXX *meta tauta* (after these things) — eschatologizing the prophecy. *epi pasan sarka* (upon all flesh) — universalizing. The young/old + male/female + dream/vision pairing democratizes prophecy. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian readings of *horaseis* (visions) as craft-sightings; preserve the prophetic-Joel surface.

verses.text: καί γε ἐπὶ τοὺς δούλους μου καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς δούλας μου ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν.
verses.translit: kai ge epi tous doulous mou kai epi tas doulas mou en tais hēmerais ekeinais ekcheō apo tou pneumatos mou, kai prophēteusousin.
verses.notes: Joel-citation continued. Slave-inclusion. Lukan addition of *kai prophēteusousin* (and they shall prophesy) at the end — not in MT/LXX Joel; Lukan emphasis on prophetic-Spirit democratization.

verses.text: καὶ δώσω τέρατα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω καὶ σημεῖα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κάτω, αἷμα καὶ πῦρ καὶ ἀτμίδα καπνοῦ·
verses.translit: kai dōsō terata en tō ouranō anō kai sēmeia epi tēs gēs katō, haima kai pyr kai atmida kapnou·
verses.notes: **MAJOR COSMIC-SIGNS VERSE**. *terata en tō ouranō anō* (wonders in the heaven above) + *sēmeia epi tēs gēs katō* (signs on the earth below). Lukan additions *anō* and *katō* + *sēmeia* (not in Joel LXX) — heightening cosmic-vertical scope. *haima kai pyr kai atmida kapnou* (blood, fire, smoke-column) — destruction-imagery. Cross-corpus Luke 21:11, 25-26; Rev 6:12-13. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: *terata en tō ouranō anō* (wonders/portents in the sky above) is engaged in heterodox traditions including the Raëlian canon as sky-craft signs. Preserve the prophetic-Joel surface; do not pre-resolve.

verses.text: ὁ ἥλιος μεταστραφήσεται εἰς σκότος καὶ ἡ σελήνη εἰς αἷμα πρὶν ἐλθεῖν ἡμέραν κυρίου τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ἐπιφανῆ.
verses.translit: ho hēlios metastraphēsetai eis skotos kai hē selēnē eis haima prin elthein hēmeran kyriou tēn megalēn kai epiphanē.
verses.notes: **SOLAR/LUNAR ECLIPSE-IMAGERY**. Sun darkened + moon to blood. Cross-corpus Joel 2:31 LXX; Isa 13:10; Ezek 32:7; Mark 13:24; Luke 21:25; Rev 6:12. *epiphanē* (manifest / glorious) — LXX Joel reads *epiphanē*; some witnesses substitute *emphanē* (visible). The lunar-eclipse 'blood moon' phrasing is a recurring apocalyptic topos. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve.

verses.text: καὶ ἔσται πᾶς ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται.
verses.translit: kai estai pas hos an epikalesētai to onoma kyriou sōthēsetai.
verses.notes: JOEL-CITATION CLOSE. *pas hos an epikalesētai to onoma kyriou sōthēsetai* (all who call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved) — cross-corpus Rom 10:13 (Pauline citation). The *kyrios* — in Joel LXX the divine name; in Acts re-applied to Jesus (cf. vv.36, 38). Soteriological hinge of the speech.

verses.text: Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, ἀκούσατε τοὺς λόγους τούτους. Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον, ἄνδρα ἀποδεδειγμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς δυνάμεσι καὶ τέρασι καὶ σημείοις οἷς ἐποίησεν δι’ αὐτοῦ ὁ θεὸς ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν, καθὼς αὐτοὶ οἴδατε,
verses.translit: Andres Israēlitai, akousate tous logous toutous. Iēsoun ton Nazōraion, andra apodedeigmenon apo tou theou eis hymas dynamesi kai terasi kai sēmeiois hois epoiēsen di’ autou ho theos en mesō hymōn, kathōs autoi oidate,
verses.notes: **KERYGMATIC CORE — JESUS DESCRIPTION**. *Iēsoun ton Nazōraion* (Jesus of Nazareth — alternative form to *Nazarēnos*). *andra apodedeigmenon apo tou theou* (a man attested/marked-out by God) — striking *andra* (man) framing. Some have read this as evidence of pre-Pauline 'adoptionist' Christology in early Jerusalem-tradition (Dunn 1980; Hurtado 2003). Triadic *dynameis + terata + sēmeia* (deeds-of-power + wonders + signs) for Jesus' ministry.

verses.text: τοῦτον τῇ ὡρισμένῃ βουλῇ καὶ προγνώσει τοῦ θεοῦ ἔκδοτον διὰ χειρὸς ἀνόμων προσπήξαντες ἀνείλατε,
verses.translit: touton tē hōrismenē boulē kai prognōsei tou theou ekdoton dia cheiros anomōn prospēxantes aneilate,
verses.notes: *hōrismenē boulē kai prognōsei* (determined purpose and foreknowledge) — divine-determination + human-responsibility tension. *dia cheiros anomōn* (by the hand of lawless ones) — likely the Romans (Gentiles outside Torah). *prospēxantes* (having fastened / nailed) — the crucifixion-act.

verses.text: ὃν ὁ θεὸς ἀνέστησεν λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ θανάτου, καθότι οὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν κρατεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: hon ho theos anestēsen lysas tas ōdinas tou thanatou, kathoti ouk ēn dynaton krateisthai auton hyp’ autou·
verses.notes: **RESURRECTION CLAIM**. *lysas tas ōdinas tou thanatou* (loosing the birth-pangs of death) — *ōdines* normally = childbirth-pains; LXX Ps 17:5 (18:5 MT) reads *ōdines thanatou* where MT has *chevlei mavet* (cords of death), apparently from Hebrew *chevel* (a homograph cord/labor-pain). The death-as-labor metaphor is striking — death cannot hold the one whose birth (resurrection) is determined. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian readings of the resurrection.

verses.text: Δαυὶδ γὰρ λέγει εἰς αὐτόν· Προορώμην τὸν κύριον ἐνώπιόν μου διὰ παντός, ὅτι ἐκ δεξιῶν μού ἐστιν ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῶ.
verses.translit: Dauid gar legei eis auton· Proorōmēn ton kyrion enōpion mou dia pantos, hoti ek dexiōn mou estin hina mē saleuthō.
verses.notes: PS 16:8 LXX (15:8 MT) CITATION begins. Davidic-prophetic frame for resurrection. Peter's pesher-method: David is read as prophesying about the Messiah.

verses.text: διὰ τοῦτο ηὐφράνθη ἡ καρδία μου καὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο ἡ γλῶσσά μου, ἔτι δὲ καὶ ἡ σάρξ μου κατασκηνώσει ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι·
verses.translit: dia touto ēuphranthē hē kardia mou kai ēgalliasato hē glōssa mou, eti de kai hē sarx mou kataskēnōsei ep’ elpidi·
verses.notes: Ps 16:9 LXX. *hē sarx mou kataskēnōsei ep’ elpidi* (my flesh will dwell/encamp in hope) — bodily-hope framing. LXX *glōssa* (tongue) renders MT *kavod* (glory) — likely Hebrew variant reading *kvedi* (my liver, as seat of emotion).

verses.text: ὅτι οὐκ ἐγκαταλείψεις τὴν ψυχήν μου εἰς ᾅδην, οὐδὲ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν.
verses.translit: hoti ouk enkataleipseis tēn psychēn mou eis hadēn, oude dōseis ton hosion sou idein diaphthoran.
verses.notes: Ps 16:10 LXX. *ouk enkataleipseis tēn psychēn mou eis hadēn* (will not abandon my soul to Hades). *ton hosion sou idein diaphthoran* (your holy one to see corruption). LXX *diaphthoran* (corruption) renders MT *shachat* (pit) — the Greek reading is what allows Peter's argument from non-decay. The pesher-engine of Peter's speech depends on the LXX rendering.

verses.text: ἐγνώρισάς μοι ὁδοὺς ζωῆς, πληρώσεις με εὐφροσύνης μετὰ τοῦ προσώπου σου.
verses.translit: egnōrisas moi hodous zōēs, plērōseis me euphrosynēs meta tou prosōpou sou.
verses.notes: Ps 16:11 LXX. *hodous zōēs* (ways of life) — life-paths revealed. Closes the Davidic-citation.

verses.text: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐξὸν εἰπεῖν μετὰ παρρησίας πρὸς ὑμᾶς περὶ τοῦ πατριάρχου Δαυίδ, ὅτι καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν καὶ ἐτάφη καὶ τὸ μνῆμα αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ἐν ἡμῖν ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης·
verses.translit: Andres adelphoi, exon eipein meta parrēsias pros hymas peri tou patriarchou Dauid, hoti kai eteleutēsen kai etaphē kai to mnēma autou estin en hēmin achri tēs hēmeras tautēs·
verses.notes: **PESHER-ARGUMENT PIVOT**. David's tomb (*to mnēma*) is still here — therefore David's Ps 16 must refer prophetically to another. Josephus *Ant.* 7.392-394 confirms a Davidic tomb in Jerusalem in the 1st c. CE. *parrēsias* (boldness / frankness) — Lukan-Acts keyword.

verses.text: προφήτης οὖν ὑπάρχων, καὶ εἰδὼς ὅτι ὅρκῳ ὤμοσεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς ἐκ καρποῦ τῆς ὀσφύος αὐτοῦ καθίσαι ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: prophētēs oun hyparchōn, kai eidōs hoti horkō ōmosen autō ho theos ek karpou tēs osphyos autou kathisai epi ton thronon autou,
verses.notes: Cross-corpus 2 Sam 7:12-16 + Ps 132:11 (the Davidic dynastic-oath). *ek karpou tēs osphyos* (from the fruit of his loins) — descendant. Some Byzantine + Western witnesses expand: "to raise up the Christ in flesh according to the flesh and set him upon his throne" — likely 2nd-c. theological gloss.

verses.text: προϊδὼν ἐλάλησεν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ χριστοῦ ὅτι οὔτε ἐγκατελείφθη εἰς ᾅδην οὔτε ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ εἶδεν διαφθοράν.
verses.translit: proidōn elalēsen peri tēs anastaseōs tou christou hoti oute enkateleiphthē eis hadēn oute hē sarx autou eiden diaphthoran.
verses.notes: *proidōn* (foreseeing) — Davidic prophecy. Peter's pesher resolves the Ps 16:10 puzzle by referring it to the Messiah's resurrection.

verses.text: τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνέστησεν ὁ θεός, οὗ πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν μάρτυρες.
verses.translit: touton ton Iēsoun anestēsen ho theos, hou pantes hēmeis esmen martyres.
verses.notes: WITNESS-FORMULA. *pantes hēmeis esmen martyres* (all of us are witnesses). Lukan-Acts apostolic-witness keynote (cf. 1:8, 22; 3:15; 5:32; 10:39; 13:31).

verses.text: τῇ δεξιᾷ οὖν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑψωθεὶς τήν τε ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου λαβὼν παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐξέχεεν τοῦτο ὃ ὑμεῖς καὶ βλέπετε καὶ ἀκούετε.
verses.translit: tē dexia oun tou theou hypsōtheis tēn te epangelian tou pneumatos tou hagiou labōn para tou patros execheen touto ho hymeis kai blepete kai akouete.
verses.notes: **EXALTATION-CLAIM**. *tē dexia tou theou hypsōtheis* — ambiguous: (a) instrumental dative "by the right hand of God exalted" or (b) locative "to the right hand of God exalted." Modern critical reading prefers (b). Cross-corpus Ps 110:1 (cf. Acts 2:34-35 below). *execheen* (poured out) — same root as Joel 2:28 *ekcheō* in v.17.

verses.text: οὐ γὰρ Δαυὶδ ἀνέβη εἰς τοὺς οὐρανούς, λέγει δὲ αὐτός· Εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου,
verses.translit: ou gar Dauid anebē eis tous ouranous, legei de autos· Eipen ho kyrios tō kyriō mou· Kathou ek dexiōn mou,
verses.notes: **PS 110:1 LXX (109:1 MT) CITATION**. The most-cited HB text in the NT. *eipen ho kyrios tō kyriō mou* (the Lord said to my Lord) — the classic two-Lords puzzle, here resolved Christologically. Same pesher-argument as v.29 (David's tomb): David cannot be the *kyrios* who ascended.

verses.text: ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.
verses.translit: heōs an thō tous echthrous sou hypopodion tōn podōn sou.
verses.notes: Ps 110:1 LXX continued. *hypopodion tōn podōn* (footstool of feet) — ANE royal-conquest imagery; cf. the Tutankhamun footstool with enemies carved beneath. Cross-corpus 1 Cor 15:25; Heb 1:13; 10:13.

verses.text: ἀσφαλῶς οὖν γινωσκέτω πᾶς οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι καὶ κύριον αὐτὸν καὶ χριστὸν ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός, τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε.
verses.translit: asphalōs oun ginōsketō pas oikos Israēl hoti kai kyrion auton kai christon epoiēsen ho theos, touton ton Iēsoun hon hymeis estaurōsate.
verses.notes: **KERYGMATIC CLIMAX**. *kai kyrion auton kai christon epoiēsen ho theos* (God made him both Lord and Christ). The *epoiēsen* (made) verb is the classic 'adoptionist-sounding' moment of early-Jerusalem kerygma — read by Dunn 1980 and others as preserving pre-Pauline Christology. The contrast *epoiēsen ho theos … hymeis estaurōsate* (God made him … YOU crucified him) is the speech's rhetorical climax.

verses.text: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ κατενύγησαν τὴν καρδίαν, εἶπόν τε πρὸς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς ἀποστόλους· Τί ποιήσωμεν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί;
verses.translit: Akousantes de katenygēsan tēn kardian, eipon te pros ton Petron kai tous loipous apostolous· Ti poiēsōmen, andres adelphoi?
verses.notes: *katenygēsan tēn kardian* (cut to the heart) — vivid penetration-image. *Ti poiēsōmen* (what shall we do?) — soteriological-response question, structurally important for Acts (cf. 16:30 jailer's question).

verses.text: Πέτρος δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Μετανοήσατε, καὶ βαπτισθήτω ἕκαστος ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ εἰς ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ὑμῶν, καὶ λήμψεσθε τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος·
verses.translit: Petros de pros autous· Metanoēsate, kai baptisthētō hekastos hymōn epi tō onomati Iēsou christou eis aphesin tōn hamartiōn hymōn, kai lēmpsesthe tēn dōrean tou hagiou pneumatos·
verses.notes: **BAPTISMAL-FORMULA SITE**. *Metanoēsate, kai baptisthētō hekastos hymōn epi tō onomati Iēsou christou eis aphesin tōn hamartiōn hymōn* (repent and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for forgiveness of sins). Singular-name baptism (vs. triadic Matt 28:19) — text-critical evidence for early one-name Jewish-Christian practice. *epi tō onomati* (in/upon the name) vs. Matthew's *eis to onoma* (into the name). **HIGH LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward (a) trinitarian-baptism harmonization or (b) Raëlian readings of repentance/baptism as transmission-related-ritual; preserve.

verses.text: ὑμῖν γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς εἰς μακράν, ὅσους ἂν προσκαλέσηται κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν.
verses.translit: hymin gar estin hē epangelia kai tois teknois hymōn kai pasi tois eis makran, hosous an proskalesētai kyrios ho theos hēmōn.
verses.notes: *tois eis makran* (those who are far off) — cross-corpus Isa 57:19 LXX; cf. Eph 2:13, 17. Hint of Gentile-inclusion to come (Acts 10-11).

verses.text: ἑτέροις τε λόγοις πλείοσιν διεμαρτύρατο, καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτοὺς λέγων· Σώθητε ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς τῆς σκολιᾶς ταύτης.
verses.translit: heterois te logois pleiosin diemartyrato, kai parekalei autous legōn· Sōthēte apo tēs geneas tēs skolias tautēs.
verses.notes: *sōthēte apo tēs geneas tēs skolias tautēs* (be saved from this crooked generation) — cross-corpus Deut 32:5 LXX *genea skolia*; cf. Phil 2:15. Summary-statement of Lukan speech-style.

verses.text: οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀποδεξάμενοι τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθησαν, καὶ προσετέθησαν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ψυχαὶ ὡσεὶ τρισχίλιαι.
verses.translit: hoi men oun apodexamenoi ton logon autou ebaptisthēsan, kai prosetethēsan en tē hēmera ekeinē psychai hōsei trischiliai.
verses.notes: *psychai hōsei trischiliai* (about three thousand souls). Lukan numerology: cf. Exod 32:28 LXX where 3000 Israelites die at the Golden Calf — a possible inverse-typology (Pentecost as new-Sinai gathering vs. Sinai's apostasy-judgment).

verses.text: ἦσαν δὲ προσκαρτεροῦντες τῇ διδαχῇ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῇ κοινωνίᾳ, τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς.
verses.translit: ēsan de proskarterountes tē didachē tōn apostolōn kai tē koinōnia, tē klasei tou artou kai tais proseuchais.
verses.notes: **FOUR-FOLD SUMMARY** of early-community life: (1) apostles' teaching; (2) *koinōnia* (fellowship / sharing); (3) *klasei tou artou* (breaking of bread — eucharistic and/or table-fellowship); (4) prayers. Idealized portrait. Cross-corpus 1QS 6:2-8 (Qumran community-rule).

verses.text: ἐγίνετο δὲ πάσῃ ψυχῇ φόβος, πολλά τε τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο.
verses.translit: egineto de pasē psychē phobos, polla te terata kai sēmeia dia tōn apostolōn egineto.
verses.notes: *phobos* (awe / fear) + signs-and-wonders through the apostles. Continuation of the Lukan signs-theme.

verses.text: πάντες δὲ οἱ πιστεύοντες ἦσαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ εἶχον ἅπαντα κοινά,
verses.translit: pantes de hoi pisteuontes ēsan epi to auto kai eichon hapanta koina,
verses.notes: **COMMON-PROPERTY IDEALIZATION**. *eichon hapanta koina* (held all things in common). Cross-corpus Plato *Republic* 5.464; Pythagorean *koina ta tōn philōn*; 1QS 6:19-23 (Qumran community-property); cf. Acts 4:32-35. The Lukan-Acts ideal of property-sharing is structurally repeated in Lukan-Acts summaries.

verses.text: καὶ τὰ κτήματα καὶ τὰς ὑπάρξεις ἐπίπρασκον καὶ διεμέριζον αὐτὰ πᾶσιν καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν·
verses.translit: kai ta ktēmata kai tas hyparxeis epipraskon kai diemerizon auta pasin kathoti an tis chreian eichen·
verses.notes: *kathoti an tis chreian eichen* (according as anyone had need) — the famous distribution-by-need principle. Cross-corpus 4:34-35; cf. the inverse Marxist appropriation ("from each according to ability, to each according to need").

verses.text: καθ’ ἡμέραν τε προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, κλῶντές τε κατ’ οἶκον ἄρτον, μετελάμβανον τροφῆς ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει καὶ ἀφελότητι καρδίας,
verses.translit: kath’ hēmeran te proskarterountes homothymadon en tō hierō, klōntes te kat’ oikon arton, metelambanon trophēs en agalliasei kai aphelotēti kardias,
verses.notes: *homothymadon* (with one accord) — Lukan-Acts community keyword (1:14; 4:24; 5:12; etc.). Temple-attendance + house-table fellowship — dual locus. *aphelotēti* (simplicity / sincerity) — hapax in NT.

verses.text: αἰνοῦντες τὸν θεὸν καὶ ἔχοντες χάριν πρὸς ὅλον τὸν λαόν. ὁ δὲ κύριος προσετίθει τοὺς σῳζομένους καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.
verses.translit: ainountes ton theon kai echontes charin pros holon ton laon. ho de kyrios prosetithei tous sōzomenous kath’ hēmera epi to auto.
verses.notes: **CHAPTER-CLOSING SUMMARY**. *charin pros holon ton laon* (favor with all the people). *ho kyrios prosetithei tous sōzomenous* (the Lord was adding those being saved). Chapter ends with growth-statement; Lukan-distinctive *prosetithei* growth-verb (cf. 2:41; 5:14; 11:24).
